intent: Reinstall the 54 packages captured by phone_backup.sh onto the freshly wiped Pixel 6a without disturbing the device owner, which cannot be re-provisioned once any account exists.
scope: Non-goal: app-private data, logins, Signal history -- unreachable from adb on an unrooted phone
Non-goal: Google 'Copy apps & data', which is setup-wizard-only and mutually exclusive with device owner provisioning
changes: New restore_apps.sh: iterates the backup's per-package directories and installs each with `adb install-multiple`, since 130 APKs across 54 packages means splits and `adb install base.apk` fails on those with INSTALL_FAILED_INVALID_APK.

Failures are collected and summarised rather than aborting the run: preinstalled and Play-licensed packages are expected to refuse a sideload, and stop-on-first-error would leave the restore half-done with no report.

com.kuhy.focus_owner is skipped by name. The captured APK is the old debug-signed build; it could not install over the provisioned release build anyway, but a successful downgrade would be far worse than a failed one.
Device owner state is printed before and after the run, so the invariant the whole factory reset was spent on is checked rather than assumed.

verification.evidence: Clean after splitting the SC2155 declare-and-assign on SCRIPT_NAME.
54 packages enumerated, split counts correct (airbnb 9, claude 6, discord 6), and 'SKIP com.kuhy.focus_owner (device owner; keeping the provisioned build)'.
Installed: 54  Failed: 0. Better than predicted -- no Play-licensed refusals materialised. `pm list packages -3 | wc -l` on device confirms 54.
DCIM 1.2G (6 files), Download 40 files, Pictures 43 files, Movies 4, Music 2. On-device du: 1.1G DCIM, 109M Download, 4.3M Pictures.
27 images indexed in MediaStore. The documented MEDIA_MOUNTED broadcast is rejected by modern Android (SecurityException); scan_volume is the working path.

verification.command: dumpsys device_policy + dumpsys account after the full restore
verification.evidence: Device Owner Type: 0, admin=ComponentInfo{...FocusDeviceAdminReceiver}, accounts: 0. The restore cost nothing.

risks: Once a Google account is added, `dpm set-device-owner` can never run again without another factory reset. The escape hatch still releases without a wipe, but it becomes ONE-WAY: releasing means losing device owner permanently. The plan to 're-test the release path after each restriction' is therefore no longer safe to execute literally; verify the path is reachable (isDeviceOwner true, button rendered) instead of pressing it.

No .kdbx was found on /sdcard, before or after. KeePassDX stores its database in private storage, so phone_backup.sh never captured it. The canonical copy is on the PC, which is the user's stated intent.
App-private data did not come back: every app is at first-run state, and all logins must be redone. Signal history was destroyed by the wipe with the user's explicit go-ahead.
restore_apps.sh has no automated tests. It is an adb-driven operational script in phone_focus_mode/, matching the existing untested scripts there; the dry-run mode is the safety mechanism.
rollback: Uninstall any unwanted package with `adb uninstall <pkg>`; nothing here is destructive to the device owner.
NEVER `adb uninstall com.kuhy.focus_owner` while it holds device ownership -- releasing first from inside the app is the only safe order, and after an account exists the release cannot be undone.
